# tenant-value API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Historical tenant-value serialization and OData string-literal escaping.

## deserializeTenantValue

Parses stored text as JSON, falling back to the unchanged string when parsing fails. JSON-like strings become primitives, bigint decimal strings can lose precision as numbers, and Dates remain text. T is only a compile-time assertion: no schema validation, Date reconstruction or runtime type checking occurs.

### Imports

```ts
import { deserializeTenantValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { deserializeTenantValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when

- You read historical tenant text and can validate its JSON-first interpretation in the caller.

### Avoid when

- You need a schema-validated or lossless type round trip; validate the unknown result in the caller.

### Examples

```tsx
import { deserializeTenantValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const value = deserializeTenantValue<unknown>('false'); // boolean false
```

### Type

```ts
function deserializeTenantValue<T>
```

### Signatures

```ts
<T>(rawValue: string): T
```

#### Type parameters

- `T`: Expected result type; callers must validate untrusted data.

#### Parameters

- `rawValue`: Stored string to parse.

#### Returns

Parsed JSON value, or original string when parsing fails.

## escapeODataValue

Doubles single quotes for the content of an OData string literal. This does not add surrounding quotes, escape a full query or encode a URL.

### Imports (2)

```ts
import { escapeODataValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { escapeODataValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (2)

- You embed user text inside an OData single-quoted string literal.

### Examples (2)

```ts
import { escapeODataValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const filter = `key eq '${escapeODataValue("owner's-settings")}'`;
```

### Signatures (2)

```ts
(value: string): string
```

#### Parameters (2)

- `value`: Raw string-literal content.

#### Returns (2)

Content with each single quote doubled.

## serializeTenantValue

Converts a tenant-store value into a string: primitives become String(value), Date uses ISO text, and other values use JSON.stringify with a String fallback when JSON returns undefined. Legacy null input becomes the literal null string. Circular objects, nested BigInts and invalid Dates can throw.

### Imports (3)

```ts
import { serializeTenantValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { serializeTenantValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/helpers';
```

### Use when (3)

- You must preserve the historical standalone tenant-value string format.

### Avoid when (2)

- You write new list-store values and need exact empty/JSON-like strings or bigint text; use the tenant/site store service encoding instead.

### Throws

- Native serialization errors for unsupported JSON values or invalid Dates.

### Examples (3)

#### Basic usage

```ts
import { serializeTenantValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

const stored = serializeTenantValue({ enabled: true });
```

#### Compare legacy serialization with validated unknown data

```ts
import { serializeTenantValue, deserializeTenantValue, escapeODataValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
const filter = `Title eq '${escapeODataValue("owner's-settings")}'`;
// Title eq 'owner''s-settings'
const raw = serializeTenantValue({ enabled: true });
const value = deserializeTenantValue<unknown>(raw);
if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== undefined && value !== null) console.log(value);
const legacy = deserializeTenantValue<unknown>('false'); // boolean false
```

### Signatures (3)

```ts
(value: unknown): string
```

#### Parameters (3)

- `value`: Value to serialize without a schema.

#### Returns (3)

Stored text; serialization is not lossless for every input type.
